title: Why Was the Only Japanese Titanic Survivor Shamed? 🤯
description: Masabumi Hosono was the only Japanese passenger on the Titanic. After surviving the 1912 disaster, he returned home to face public shaming and the loss of his career.

beats.text: Masabumi Hosono jumped into one of the Titanic’s last lifeboats.
beats.visual: photograph of Masabumi Hosono in a suit, 1912

beats.text: The civil servant was the only passenger from his nation.
beats.visual: photograph of the RMS Titanic departing Southampton, 1912

beats.text: When a crew member called for more, Hosono stepped forward.
beats.visual: illustration of Titanic lifeboats being lowered at night, 1912

beats.text: After his rescue, he wrote his story on Titanic stationery.
beats.visual: photograph of original RMS Titanic letterhead stationery

beats.text: But back in Japan, the press branded his survival a disgrace.
beats.visual: Japanese newspaper front page from nineteen twelve

beats.text: He was fired for failing to die honorably with the ship.
beats.visual: photograph of the Shiodome freight terminal railway office, 1910s

beats.text: For the rest of his life, he regretted that leap.
beats.visual: portrait of Masabumi Hosono in later life, 1930s
